spawn_side_FALSE_LEAD_RULED_OUT.correction: ⚠️ RULED OUT on closer verification. debugger.functionBounds on 0x8005a1d8 shows it is NOT inside primary contact_alloc (0x80059e44, functionEnd 0x8005a0dc) at all -- it is inside a SEPARATE, adjacent 'sibling' allocator (0x8005a0e0-0x8005a304), already flagged as existing in FUNC_80059E44's own source comment ('Also fcn.8005a0e0, sibling w/ explicit transform args') but never before traced. Disassembling primary contact_alloc's own body (0x80059e44-0x8005a0d8) confirms it calls ONLY 0x800593e8 (render-attr helper) and 0x80024ddc (post-init) -- it never calls the sibling. A direct memory read of metadata table row ctorType=49 (0x8007941c + 49*0x14 = 0x800797f0) confirms action_id=1 there, NOT 118 -- so the 0x80056de4/FUNC_800563D4 call site (documented separately in ObsidianVault/Canon/Functions/FUNC_800563D4_actor_skinned_update.md) is a real, gated contact spawn but produces a DIFFERENT, unidentified effect (action_id=1), not the web. spawn_side_CORRECTED_2026-08-02.method: Reloaded the movie fresh, cleared breakpoints, armed an execute breakpoint directly at the sibling allocator's own write instruction (0x8005a1d8) and looped movie.advanceToFrame + debugger.resume, reading $v0 (the value about to be stored, since 0x8005a1d0 'lhu v0,0(a1)' already executed by the time the breakpoint halts at the next instruction), $ra, $a1, and $s0 (destination record pointer) at every hit through the first two confirmed hit windows.
spawn_side_CORRECTED_2026-08-02.result: Two real spawn events found: movie-relative frame 78 (v0=118, s0=0x800b1450 -> pool slot 33) and frame 168 (v0=118, s0=0x800b1530 -> pool slot 37) -- both well BEFORE their corresponding health-drop events (f312, f604), consistent with a slow-traveling tracked projectile (matching the independently-confirmed closing-distance behavior in walker_dispatch_side above). BOTH hits share the identical caller ($ra=0x8004a400, i.e. call instruction at 0x8004a3f8) and the identical a1=0x80079da4 -- a FIXED metadata-row pointer, not an index into the global ctorType table. Read directly: *(0x80079da4) = action_id 118 (0x76), active_type 60 -- confirms this fixed row, not table-index 49, is the true source of the web's action_id.

real_spawn_caller_0x8004a2b0.method: debugger.functionBounds on the call instruction (0x8004a3f8) resolves to an UNNAMED function, 0x8004a2b0-0x8004a428 (380 bytes; debugger.resolveSymbol returns no name). Disassembled the function in full.
real_spawn_caller_0x8004a2b0.result: Structure: (1) s0=*(a0+4); if the halfword at s0+0x4a is nonzero, EXIT immediately (a suppress/already-active gate). (2) A per-candidate COOLDOWN byte at (*(s0+0x80))+0xf is decremented each call; only when it reaches exactly 0 does the function proceed AND reset the cooldown to a semi-randomized value in [40,103] (via a rotating byte-stream cursor at 0x800822f4, masked to 6 bits + 40) -- i.e. a randomized per-candidate attack cooldown, not a fixed timer or tight proximity check. (3) Computes dx,dz from the CANDIDATE's own position fields (s0+4, s0+0xc -- the standard actor-record position offsets used throughout this project) to Flik's position (0x800A6500/0x800A6508), calls an atan2-style helper (0x80060ae4) to get the angle toward Flik, and uses that angle (with a stored 'last facing' snap/clamp against s0+0x14) to compute the spawn direction via the same sin/cos LUT (0x80074970) seen elsewhere. (4) Calls the sibling allocator (0x8005a0e0) with the FIXED metadata pointer 0x80079da4, producing the action_id=118 web record. (5) Immediately afterward calls 0x8005044c(a0=25, a1=s0+4) -- almost certainly the web's own SFX trigger (SFX id 25), a free, direct answer to the row's open cross-system/audio item.
real_spawn_caller_0x8004a2b0.a0_is_scratch_not_actor: IMPORTANT: live-traced a0 at the function's own entry breakpoint and found it is a FIXED CALLER-OWNED STACK ADDRESS (0x801ffea8), not a persistent actor-table pointer -- reading a0+0x80/+0x6e/+0x5c from it returns stack garbage (a stale type-word 0x40, hp -12, and rapidly-cycling flags), confirming a0 is a small scratch buffer the (not-yet-identified) CALLER fills in per candidate before invoking this utility, not the daddy-long-legs' own persistent record. This function is called on a strict 4-frame cadence (hit at movie-relative frames 0,4,8...96 in one trace) -- consistent with being invoked from a generic per-tick 'evaluate ranged-attack candidates' scheduler, with s0=*(a0+4) refreshed by that (unidentified) caller each tick.
real_spawn_caller_0x8004a2b0.indirect_dispatch: debugger.xrefsTo on 0x8004a2b0 found only ONE weak 'data'-type reference (a computed lui/addiu address, not a plain jal instruction) -- meaning this function is reached via an indirect call (a function-pointer/callback field), not a literal jal from a fixed caller. This is architecturally IDENTICAL to a pattern another concurrent Phase-4 row (D07_mosquitoes) independently documented the same session: 'Mosquito family is actor id 10 with optional callback +0x7C = 0x8004A180'. The strong working hypothesis is that daddy-long-legs' own actor record carries an equivalent optional callback (plausibly the same +0x7C slot) pointing at 0x8004a2b0, assigned per-species at spawn-table init rather than gated by a hard-coded id check anywhere in the callback body itself.
